target_customer: Teens who make polls, with brands and influencers as intended paying users for consumer feedback
problem: Teens wanted a light way to ask friends questions on Snapchat, and brands wanted to hear from teens.
business_model: Free consumer app; planned monetization via brands and influencers running polls

founders.name: Ranidu Lankage
founders.background_notes: YC page and search coverage of TechCrunch name The Drop and Whale; later he worked on Audius.

founders.name: James Zhang
founders.background_notes: YC blog 2017 calls him CTO. His YC profile lists Stripe and Notion; those may postdate Polly.

founders.name: Vicc Alexander
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as head of mobile and design and as a Whale co-founder with Justin Kan.

competitors.name: Sarahah
competitors.what: Anonymous feedback app that spread through Snapchat
competitors.traction_then: Rising teen app in 2017, criticized as ready made for cyberbullying

competitors.name: tbh
competitors.what: Anonymous positive poll app for teens

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile polling app with Snapchat sharing, but scaling to millions of votes a day and moderation need solid engineering.

defensibility.rationale: The idea was copied within weeks, and The Next Web reported Instagram copying a popular Snapchat add on like Polly on 2017-10-03.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Polly depended on Snapchat for distribution. The Next Web titled an October 2017 article about Instagram copying the popular Snapchat add on Polly; the article was not opened.

market_need_then: The YC launch post reports 20 million people voting over 100 million times across 5 million polls in the past month, and top 15 social app ranks in many countries.

branding.domain_note: Listed website polly.fun; not fetchable from this session. Not an exact match .com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Fun and light, per the YC launch post title

branding.community_and_virality: Spread among teens on Snapchat per TechCrunch and Ypulse 2017 coverage, with Common Sense Media and Protect Young Eyes reviews of the app.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong short term teen usage and press in 2017, but the name collides with Polly for Slack and Polly Pocket, and nothing shows lasting brand pull.

pivots.why: YC blog says the Whale team pivoted into Polly during the summer program; the exact month is not stated

outcome_analysis: Polly grew very fast in 2017 as a Snapchat linked polling app, with a reported 20 million voters in a month, built by the Whale team after a pivot. The YC directory marks it inactive, but no source explains why or when it stopped, and no funding was found for this app, so the cause is not public. The risks visible at the time were reliance on Snapchat and fast copying by larger platforms, which are noted in the competition fields but are not confirmed as the cause.
notes: polly.fun failed DNS in this session, so the site is treated as unreachable. Funding search found only Polly of Seattle (Slack polling bot, 1.2M seed and 7M round), a different company, which is excluded. The YC page shows founded 2015, which reflects Whale. The Next Web item on Instagram copying was seen only as a search title.
